candidates.changed_node: CS_RANK(MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 0)) * CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42)) -> CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage, 126)) * TS_RANK($volume, 21); removed the MAX(...,0) gate (only free constant), the $high/$low correlation kernel (2 fields), and the redundant CS_DEMEAN
candidates.rationale: Keeps the parent's idea: quality rank penalised by levering-up, weighted by trading pressure. Three simplifications. (1) CS_DEMEAN around a CS_RANK is a per-day constant shift, so it is cross-sectionally identical and free to drop. (2) The MAX(...,0) one-sided gate goes, taking the only free constant with it (1 -> 0). (3) The two-field TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42) comovement kernel collapses to the volume field alone (fields 5 -> 3, 113 -> 72 chars, depth stays 5). The leverage-growth gate is kept because it is what separates the parent from the already-archived CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) - CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 15)); dropping it instead would restate that member. Window moved 63 -> 126 by necessity, not taste: every single-operator wrapper on TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) (CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE, ABS, MAX, unary minus) is already a 4-node archive block, and the round-5 attempt CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) * CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high - $low, 42)) died sharing 7 nodes with this parent. A 126-day fundamental delta clears coverage - RANK(TS_DELTA($roa, 126)) is an accepted archive member. IC should hold: the roe leg is the workhorse, the two-quarter leverage change is a smoother read of the same balance-sheet expansion, and CS_RANK(fundamental) * TS_RANK(volume) is the pattern behind this island's best fitnesses. Residual risk is the correlation gate, since the roe leg dominates rho and this family already holds two members; the 63 -> 126 switch is the lever that took a comparable attempt from 0.906 to 0.800.

candidates.changed_node: CS_RANK(($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8)) -> TS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 5), 42); removed the $high/$low/$open normalised-range leg (depth 6 -> 5, fields 5 -> 3) and the redundant CS_DEMEAN
candidates.rationale: Same idea kept: quality rank minus signed leverage growth scaled by a fast volatility state. The depth-6 leg CS_RANK(($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8)) is a three-field normalised range; replacing it with a one-field within-name volatility percentile takes fields 5 -> 3 and depth 6 -> 5, and the redundant CS_DEMEAN goes for free (constants were already 0). CS_ZSCORE is retained on the leverage leg so the penalty stays signed - deleveraging still adds - which is the parent's asymmetry against its sibling. The delta window has to move off 63 because CS_ZSCORE(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) is this parent's own 4-node block and would trip archive_subtree immediately; 126 is the same window that carried a prior attempt from 0.906 down to 0.800 on the correlation gate. Volatility is expressed as TS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 5), 42) rather than a cross-sectional vol rank on purpose: CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 10)) and CS_RANK($roe) - TS_RANK($high - $low, 10) are both archive members, so a cross-sectional vol term or any TS_RANK of the raw range would land on top of them, whereas a within-name percentile of short-horizon vol is a different cross-section. Half-life should stay short like the parent's 7.5 days. Main risk, stated plainly: this and the sibling proposal share the roe leg and the 126-day leverage delta, so if both are scored they may correlate above 0.80 with each other even if each clears the existing archive.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: SIMPLIFY. Each expression below was flagged as more complex than it needs
to be. Return a simpler expression that keeps the same idea.

Simpler means strictly fewer distinct fields, fewer free constants, or less
depth. The simplification is accepted only if it also keeps at least
80% of the parent's fit-window |IC|, so do not remove the component
doing the work. Put the parent's id in `parent_ids` and name what you removed in
`changed_node`.
